title: The MLS Wrap: Griezmann matches Messi in goal-tastic weekend
subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutTV schedulesThe MLS Wrap: Griezmann matches Messi in goal-tastic weekendShareLionel Messi lit up MLS once again with two brilliant goals for Inter Miami against Atlanta United, but the performance of another former star of the European leagues arguably eclipsed the Argentine in Matchday 31.
There are only a few weeks of the league season left to go before the playoffs begin, and we are on the verge of crowning the MLS regular season champion for 2026.
There’s also another trophy to play for this week as St. Louis City and Columbus Crew face off to see who will become US national domestic cup champions in the US Open Cup final.
Inter Miami officially secured their place in the MLS playoffs with a 2-0 win over New York City in midweek as Lionel Messi and Luis Suárez assisted goals for Rodrigo De Paul and Germán Berterame.
They followed it up this weekend with a 3-1 win against Atlanta United in Georgia, where Messi bagged a brace, Berterame scored again, and Suárez added a couple more assists to his season stats.

Messi’s magic can sometimes be taken for granted. There is no longer a surprise when looking at an Inter Miami scoreline and seeing his name mentioned multiple times among the list of goals and assists.
😮‍💨💫 Lionel Messi, Luis Suarez, and Germán Berterame were all in the goals as Inter Miami beat Atlanta 1-3 overnight. Messi keeps delivering. 👑 pic.twitter.com/WsPatY2XzK
His goals on Saturday were world-class, as he dribbled past defenders and finished with aplomb.
Though this now seems normal for Messi, it’s worth stepping back now and again to remember how impressive this all is for the 39-year-old who recently retired from international football.

Messi currently tops the charts for both goals and assists in MLS. He’s five ahead of the next most prolific goalscorer, Petar Musa, on 25, and level with Anders Dreyer, Son Heung-min, and Cristian Espinoza, on 12 assists.
MLS’s own stats definitions, which count some secondary assists, have Messi level with Son on 15 assists.
Messi has the highest average FotMob rating in MLS by some distance on 8.32, and also tops the charts for goals per 90, expected goals, shots per 90, expected assists, and xG + xA per 90.
Though Messi topping the table for all these metrics and more is not particularly unexpected, it’s sometimes worth a reminder that it’s still happening and shows no sign of slowing up.
With Messi in the league, even the biggest-name players at other teams can fly under the radar somewhat as the focus regularly lands on Inter Miami alone.
Even in the same state of Florida, there is another player who might normally be a leading light in MLS in other, non-Messi circumstances, playing his part in leading his team to a playoff spot.
Antoine Griezmann scored twice in Orlando City’s 4-1 win at home to DC United, and assisted Martín Ojeda’s outstanding strike. It was a victory that puts them more comfortably in a playoff spot.
😍💫 Perhaps the best goal you will see on your timeline this year. https://t.co/7lxqWLxGEt
Orlando have a very useful pair of wins and a draw from their last three games that could prevent them from being drawn into a tight race for the playoffs come the final games of the season.
Griezmann has 11 goals in his last nine games for Orlando, having joined the team in the summer, not far off Messi’s recent record.
His signing looks set to be one of the more successful acquisitions of an aging European star by an MLS side, and he edges Messi as the player of the round per FotMob’s ratings.
